title: Derived tensor cohomology under a flat change of ring diagram
statement:
Let $R,A,B,R_1,A_1,B_1$ be commutative rings with compatible homomorphisms $R\to A$, $R\to B$, $R\to R_1$, $A\to A_1$, $B\to B_1$, $R_1\to A_1$, and $R_1\to B_1$. Put $D=A\otimes_R B$ and $D_1=A_1\otimes_{R_1}B_1$, with their induced homomorphism $D\to D_1$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product, def-weil-module-base-change]. Suppose $R_1$ is flat over $R$, $A_1$ is flat over $A\otimes_R R_1$, and $B_1$ is flat over $R_1\otimes_R B$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. For any $M\in D(A)$, the unbounded derived category of ordinary modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], use K-flat derived tensor products [def-pc-module-kflat-complex]. The canonical scalar-extension map is an isomorphism of $D_1$-modules, for every $i\in\mathbf Z$:
$$H^i(M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}B)\otimes_D D_1\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ H^i((M\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A_1)\otimes_{R_1}^{\mathbf L}B_1).$$
On both cohomology groups the two factor-ring actions commute; these are the displayed tensor-ring module structures. The map is induced by the units of scalar extension on the two factors and extension of the base ring, followed by the $D_1$-action on cohomology. It is natural in $M$ and compatible with the augmentation maps of K-flat and free resolutions used to compute the derived tensor products. No boundedness or flatness of $A$ or $B$ over $R$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0DJD (lemma-lemma-tor-independent-flat-compare), with the hypotheses of Tag 08HW (lemma-tor-independent-flat); cohomology module actions and canonical comparison as in its proof.

proof.text: Put $A_0=A\otimes_RR_1$, $B_0=R_1\otimes_RB$ and $D_0=A_1\otimes_{R_1}B_0$. The map $A\to A_0$ is flat: for an exact sequence of $A$-modules, its tensor with $A_0$ identifies with its tensor over $R$ with $R_1$, which is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact]. The assumed flatness of $A_0\to A_1$ and [lem-pc-module-flat-transitive] therefore give flatness of $A\to A_1$. Notice the canonical ring identifications $D_0=A_1\otimes_RB=D\otimes_AA_1$ and $D_1=D_0\otimes_{B_0}B_1$; the maps send the factor generators to the indicated factor generators. No flatness of $A$ or $B$ over $R$ has entered.

Choose a complex representing $M$ and K-flat resolutions $P\to M$ over $A$ and $F\to B[0]$ over $R$, with flat terms, by [lem-pc-source-module-kflat-resolution]. Set $P_1=P\otimes_AA_1$ and $F_1=F\otimes_RR_1$. Both are K-flat over their respective new rings by [lem-pc-kflat-extension-of-scalars]. Since $R_1$ is flat over $R$, [lem-pc-flat-scalar-extension-homology-adjunct], with its $A=E=R$, $D=R_1$ and $\varphi$ the unit chain map, gives isomorphisms $R_1\otimes_RH^i(F)\cong H^i(F_1)$ and $R_1\otimes_RH^i(B[0])\cong H^i(B_0[0])$, both $r\otimes[z]\mapsto[z\otimes r]$; this formula commutes with the augmentation, so $F_1\to B_0[0]$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The K-flat scalar-extension counit [lem-pc-kflat-scalar-extension-counit] identifies $P_1$ with $X=M\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A_1$ in $D(A_1)$. These statements hold for unbounded $P,F$.

First compute with $B_0$. By [lem-pc-balanced-derived-tensor-model], $C=\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_RF)$ represents $M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}B$ and $C_0=\operatorname{Tot}(P_1\otimes_{R_1}F_1)$ represents $X\otimes_{R_1}^{\mathbf L}B_0$, with the commuting factor actions on cohomology. There is a chain isomorphism $\theta:C_0\to C\otimes_AA_1$ sending $(p\otimes a)\otimes(f\otimes r)$ to $(p\otimes f)\otimes ar$, with inverse $(p\otimes f)\otimes a\mapsto(p\otimes a)\otimes(f\otimes1)$. Balancing gives well-defined inverse maps; on bidegree $(j,k)$ both differentials are $d_P\otimes1+(-1)^j1\otimes d_F$, so they commute with the maps. Degreewise these formulas extend to the direct sums defining the total complexes. They commute with the $A_1$ action. They also commute with the endomorphisms induced by $b\in B$ on the resolved factor, by functoriality in that factor [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor]; together with the $R_1$ action this gives $B_0$-linearity on cohomology. Thus the cohomology identification is $D_0$-linear.

Flatness of $A\to A_1$ allows [lem-pc-flat-scalar-extension-homology-adjunct], with its $A=E=A$, $D=A_1$, $Q=C$ (using $A\otimes_AC=C$) and $\varphi$ the unit chain map, to identify $H^i(C)\otimes_AA_1$ with $H^i(C\otimes_AA_1)$, with map $[z]\otimes a\mapsto[z\otimes a]$. Put $T_i=H^i(M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}B)$. The balancing isomorphism $T_i\otimes_DD_0\cong T_i\otimes_AA_1$ sends $t\otimes(a\otimes b)$, writing $D_0=A_1\otimes_RB$, to $bt\otimes a$; its inverse sends $t\otimes a$ to $t\otimes(a\otimes1)$. Combining this with $H^i(\theta)^{-1}$ gives $\phi_0:T_i\otimes_DD_0\xrightarrow{\sim}H^i(X\otimes_{R_1}^{\mathbf L}B_0)$. The flat cohomology identification is natural in all chain endomorphisms; hence it respects the $B$ action as well as $A_1$, and $\phi_0$ is $D_0$-linear. Its underlying map before adjoining $D_0$ sends a class represented by $p\otimes f$ to the class of $(p\otimes1)\otimes(f\otimes1)$.

Now use the tower $R_1\to B_0\to B_1$. Restrict $X$ from $A_1$ to $R_1$ and choose a K-flat representative $K$ of it over $R_1$ with flat terms [lem-pc-source-module-kflat-resolution]. The ordinary-ring case of [lem-sfb-successive-derived-quotient-normalization] gives the canonical natural isomorphism $(X\otimes_{R_1}^{\mathbf L}B_0)\otimes_{B_0}^{\mathbf L}B_1\cong X\otimes_{R_1}^{\mathbf L}B_1$, represented by $(K\otimes_{R_1}B_0)\otimes_{B_0}B_1\to K\otimes_{R_1}B_1$, $(x\otimes s)\otimes t\mapsto x\otimes st$. Here $K\otimes_{R_1}B_0$ is K-flat over $B_0$ [lem-pc-kflat-extension-of-scalars], so by [lem-pc-kflat-scalar-extension-counit] it represents $X\otimes_{R_1}^{\mathbf L}B_0$ and its termwise extension represents the derived extension to $B_1$. Since $B_1$ is flat over $B_0$, [lem-pc-flat-scalar-extension-homology-adjunct], with its $A=R_1$, $E=B_0$, $D=B_1$, $Q=K$, identifies $H^i(K\otimes_{R_1}B_1)$ with $B_1\otimes_{B_0}H^i(K\otimes_{R_1}B_0)$ by $b\otimes[z]\mapsto b[z\otimes1]$, the canonical scalar unit. These identifications respect the $A_1$ action: multiplication by any $a\in A_1$ is an $R_1$-linear endomorphism of $X$, and naturality of both identifications commutes with its induced maps. They are also $B_1$-linear, so are $D_1$-linear for the commuting $A_1,B_1$ actions. Neither $B_0$ nor $B_1$ needs to be flat over $R_1$.

Tensor $\phi_0$ over $B_0$ with $B_1$ and use step 5. For any $D$-module $T$, the ring identification $D_1=D_0\otimes_{B_0}B_1$ gives the elementary balancing isomorphism $(T\otimes_DD_0)\otimes_{B_0}B_1\cong T\otimes_DD_1$, $(t\otimes d_0)\otimes b_1\mapsto t\otimes(d_0\otimes b_1)$, whose inverse takes $t\otimes(d_0\otimes b_1)$ to $(t\otimes d_0)\otimes b_1$. Apply it to $T_i$. The resulting $D_1$-linear isomorphism is exactly the displayed source and target of the item. This only tensors an existing isomorphism and rebrackets balanced tensor products.

Finally identify the map, not just the modules. Before extending coefficients, step 4 uses precisely the chain units $p\mapsto p\otimes1$ and $f\mapsto f\otimes1$. Since $P$ and $F$ are K-flat with flat terms, the unit normalization (1) of [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction] for $A\to A_1$ and $R\to R_1$, on the one-object site of [lem-weil-pbc-singleton-site-module-comparison], says these are the derived scalar units on the chosen models. Step 5 uses the tower isomorphism whose unit identity in [lem-sfb-successive-derived-quotient-normalization] identifies the two successive units with the unit for $R_1\to B_1$. Thus the composite before adjoining $D_1$ is the comparison induced by the ring diagram. Its $D_1$-linear extension is uniquely determined by $t\otimes d\mapsto d\,\gamma_i(t)$, so it is the map specified in the statement. The balanced-model identifications [lem-pc-balanced-derived-tensor-model] are canonical under changing resolutions and natural in $M$; [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] supplies the same naturality for the resolved coefficient. The explicit $\theta$ formula commutes with maps of augmented complexes on either factor. Hence the comparison commutes with the augmentations and changes of the K-flat resolutions, including bounded-above free resolutions, which are K-flat by [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat] (free modules are flat), and is natural in $M$.
